evidence.note: Extended recon phase reading fixtures, contracts, and tests before decomposing — grounds the milestone breakdown in understanding rather than guessing.

Five explicit TaskCreate milestones defining distinct subsystems in dependency order: scaffolding/build → next/* shims (resolution) → app router+SSR → pages router+SSG → CLI+middleware. Foundational pieces sequenced before dependent features.
TaskUpdate status transitions (in_progress→completed→next) show the milestone plan was tracked and used through execution, not just authored once.

First full test run occurs only after nearly all subsystems are written; milestones completed by functional scope coverage rather than a concrete per-milestone done-signal (fixture render / test subset passing).

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-ordered milestone plan (steps 58-62) with foundational pieces (scaffolding, module-resolution shims, dev server) sequenced before dependent features (routers, SSG, actions), and tracked those milestones to completion via TaskUpdate — clearly exceeding the flat/unordered anchor-3 and the loose anchor-5. However, milestone done-criteria were scope-based ('implement these shims/routers') rather than tied to concrete verifiable signals like a fixture app rendering or a specific test subset passing, and tests were deferred to the end (step 344) rather than gating each milestone, so it falls short of the anchor-8 requirement for concrete per-milestone done-signals. This places it at a 6.
